approved: Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would move day-to-day water management in the Australian Capital Territory from the Commonwealth to the ACT Government.
It would change the law so the ACT Government, not the Commonwealth, controls all water taken from National Land and by Commonwealth agencies in the ACT.

The amendments to the Googong Dam Act would give the ACT Executive full management of the dam's surface water, and the Water Act would be updated to cover the Googong Dam Area in a water resource plan for the ACT.
Transfer water abstraction management on National Land and by Commonwealth bodies to the ACT Government.
Give the ACT Executive powers to manage Googong Dam's surface water under ACT law.
Require the Googong Dam Area to be part of a water resource plan managed by the ACT.
The ACT Government, Commonwealth agencies, and water users in the ACT.

The speaker moved to schedule the Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 for 12:45 pm and the Commonwealth Inscribed Stock Amendment Bill 2013 for debate until 2 pm, arguing the opposition supports the stock bill but needs more time for substantive discussion on debt ceiling changes, and criticised poor time management in the chamber.

Introduced the Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, which gives the ACT government full authority to manage water abstraction including the Googong Dam, implementing obligations under the Murray-Darling Basin Plan adopted in November 2012.

Supported the ACT Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 as bipartisan implementation of the Murray-Darling Basin Plan, while criticising the government's decision to defer $650 million in water buyback funding by two years, and noted Murray-Darling Basin governments first met on the issue in 1915.

Supported the ACT Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, said the Murray-Darling Basin Plan guarantees 2,750 gigalitres of additional water returned to the basin, described the ACT's self-government since 1988 including 2011 legislation removing the federal parliament's veto over territory laws, and highlighted a community-led restoration project for the Lake Tuggeranong catchment.

Supported the bill enabling the ACT to prepare Murray-Darling Basin Plan-compliant water resource plans before current plans expire at the end of 2014, said the Basin Plan restored nearly 3,000 gigalitres of water to the system, and praised the ACT Legislative Assembly's nation-leading steps on same-sex marriage.
Thanked speakers for their contributions on the Australian Capital Territory Water Management Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 and commended it to the House.
